Lessons.Title: Drawings, Situations, and Diagrams, Oh My!
ExplanationParagraphs: Illustrative Mathematics K–5 first edition (2021), Grade 3 Unit 1 Lesson 10, is about representing equal groups with tape diagrams, building from scale-two picture graphs to drawings and only then to MULTIPLICATION EXPRESSIONS at the END of the lesson. It addresses 3.OA.A / 3.OA.A.1. The source preparation requires ONE 12-card Equal Groups deck per two students; engage students in MLR8 and reasoning discussions. The five lesson steps take 10, 15, 20, 10 and 5 minutes. Use the 2021 source Student Task Statements and blackline resources via original publisher links, without copying source artwork into Edulytics.

Warm-up — Notice and Wonder: Socks (10 minutes). The teacher displays SIX PAIRS of socks. Children notice six separate groups of TWO, explain why there are 12 socks, write one question and orally compare strategies. Allow one minute of private thinking and one minute of partner discussion. The source warm-up is human-reviewed Notice and Wonder; a bare numerical 12 does NOT certify full completion.

Activity 1 — Scaled Picture Graph to Diagram (15 minutes). Revisit Elena's first-edition 'Signs I Saw on the Way Home' graph, key one picture square means TWO signs. Stop: TWO symbols = FOUR signs. Yield: ONE = TWO. Speed Limit: THREE = SIX. Street: FIVE = TEN. The source shows a THREE-PART tape diagram labelled 2 in EACH part to explain the speed-limit category. FIRST student subtask: explain exactly HOW this diagram matches the speed-limit signs. SECOND subtask: independently draw a DIFFERENT graph category using a different tape/drawing, then compare with a partner. Preserve three equal units of two; do not grade the drawings as a mere number.

Activity 2 — Card Sort: Equal Groups (20 minutes). The original 2021 two-page blackline deck includes 12 cards A–L: situation A three bags with five footballs, B four boxes with three toy cars, D two boxes with ten doughnuts, J three bins with ten ice cubes; the other EIGHT are source drawings and tape diagrams. Original pixel inspection establishes FIVE matching groups: A–F–L for three groups of five; B–H–K for four groups of three; C–I for three groups of two (no matching story); D–G for two groups of ten; and E–J for three groups of ten. There are TWO triples and THREE pairs, NOT four triples. Each classroom pair of pupils physically sorts the original cards and explains their matches and JUSTIFIES grouping. The linked original cards were inspected from the official ZIP; teacher, not an integer grader, validates the matches. Then students create TWO separate teacher-reviewed representations from the Student Facing PDF: FOUR bags each holding TWO strawberries and FOUR hands each with FIVE fingers. The respective totals 8 and 20 are supporting numbers; drawings must exhibit 4 groups and accurate group size. Use a teacher-selected example to discuss where group boundaries occur. Keep the card set for the following lesson.

Lesson synthesis (10 minutes). The teacher shows a tape diagram with FOUR equal parts, each marked FIVE. Only NOW introduce the expression 4 × 5, point to the four groups and five objects in each, and read it as 'four groups of five'. Explain that a multiplication expression contains numbers and the multiplication symbol and represents the grouping. Do not prematurely demand written expressions in earlier activities. Then the ORIGINAL 2021 five-minute Boxes of Shirts Cool-down asks whether FOUR store boxes, each holding TEN shirts, are shown by FOUR equal tape sections each labelled TEN. The diagram matches (YES), but a teacher must review the explanation. This original teacher guide task is corroborated by a publicly available first-edition-based guide; original artwork is not copied. Any Edulytics-authored supplementary Cool-down is optional and separate. The original teacher source's optional centers are Capture Squares Stage 4 and Five in a Row Stage 7; student drawings, partner sort and teacher reflection require teacher judgment.

The three Speed Limit picture symbols represent six source road signs at a two-sign key; that means 2+2+2=6. The independent road-sign depiction and numeric answer are not evidence that the publisher's original visual has been copied.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal groups
KeyConcepts.Definition: Several distinct groups containing the SAME number of items.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check both the number of groups and items per group before interpreting a picture or diagram.
KeyConcepts.Example: Four bags with two strawberries each: four groups, two in each, eight total.

KeyConcepts.Title: Picture-graph key to tape diagram
KeyConcepts.Definition: One square in the scaled graph is mapped to one equally-sized tape part.
KeyConcepts.Rule: One symbol = two road signs, so the three speed-limit symbols become THREE parts each labelled TWO.

KeyConcepts.Title: Card sort reasoning
KeyConcepts.Definition: A drawing, diagram and story match if they have the same number of equal groups with the same count in each.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher checks all original twelve cards A–L; the number alone cannot prove two representations agree.
KeyConcepts.Example: Source-verified five groups A–F–L (3×5), B–H–K (4×3), C–I (3×2), D–G (2×10), E–J (3×10) have two triples and three pairs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Introducing multiplication expression at synthesis
KeyConcepts.Definition: A multiplication expression models group count followed by group size, introduced only at this lesson's END.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Read a × b as a groups of b in this lesson; do not force symbols before drawings are understood.
KeyConcepts.Example: 4 × 5 represents four equal tape sections, each marked five; total 20.

WorkedExamples.Title: Warm-up — six pairs of socks
WorkedExamples.Question: How many socks are in six separate pairs? What do you notice or wonder?
WorkedExamples.Method: Draw distinct groups and invite student-created observations; the teacher reviews the open part.
Steps: Draw six separate pair outlines.
Place TWO socks in every pair.
Skip count by twos to 12 or add six twos.
Explain the group structure to a partner and pose a genuine question.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 12 socks, represented by six groups of two; Notice/Wonder is teacher-reviewed.
WorkedExamples.Check: 6 × 2 = 12 is supporting arithmetic, not a compulsory symbolic answer for the warm-up.

WorkedExamples.Title: Activity 1 — scaled graph to equal tape
WorkedExamples.Question: How does the source tape model the speed-limit sign symbols? Choose a different category and represent it.
WorkedExamples.Method: Map one scaled graph square to one tape section with label 2.
Steps: Read source key: every square means TWO signs.
Count the THREE speed-limit squares.
Draw three equal sections marked TWO.
Explain 2+2+2=6; separately choose Yield, Stop or Street and draw its matching grouping.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Speed Limit = three equal groups of two, total six. Other category must show its own actual group count.
WorkedExamples.Check: Original sign symbol counts Stop 2, Yield 1, Speed 3, Street 5; each worth two. The three Speed Limit symbols give 2+2+2=6.

WorkedExamples.Title: Activity 2 — five verified original matching sets
WorkedExamples.Question: How do the 12 source cards A–L form five sets of matching story, tape and/or drawing representations?
WorkedExamples.Method: Match group COUNT and group SIZE for each situation; original 12 physical cards remain teacher-controlled.
Steps: Match A-F-L as THREE groups of FIVE (three bags with five footballs, matching picture and tape).
Match B-H-K as FOUR groups of THREE (four boxes of three cars, matching tape and drawing).
Match C-I as THREE groups of TWO, a diagram/drawing PAIR with no corresponding story card.
Match D-G as TWO groups of TEN doughnuts and E-J as THREE groups of TEN ice cubes.
Teacher verifies all TWELVE cards exactly once and asks pupils to justify all five sets; totals alone are insufficient.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Five sets: A–F–L, B–H–K, C–I, D–G, E–J.

WorkedExamples.Title: Activity 2 — two distinct source drawing tasks
WorkedExamples.Question: Make separate diagrams for four bags of two strawberries and four hands of five fingers.
WorkedExamples.Method: Create accurate group models, not just mathematical totals.
Steps: Draw four separate bag outlines and place two berries in EACH.
Count 2+2+2+2=8 berries.
Draw four separate hands/groups and place five finger marks in EACH.
Count 5+5+5+5=20 and ask a partner to inspect group structure.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Bags: four groups of two = 8. Hands: four groups of five = 20.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both original source drawing tasks must be completed independently; teacher judges each drawn model.

WorkedExamples.Title: Synthesis — first symbolic expression
WorkedExamples.Question: A four-section tape is marked five in each section. What expression does the teacher introduce?
WorkedExamples.Method: Only after card sorting and concrete models introduce the group count and group size as factors.
Steps: Count FOUR equal tape sections.
Read FIVE objects per section.
Write the teacher-introduced expression 4 × 5.
Explain the factors and interpret as 'four groups of five'.
WorkedExamples.Check: 4 × 5=20; multiplication notation is introduced in the ten-minute synthesis, not at the start.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original Boxes of Shirts Cool-down — justify a tape match
WorkedExamples.Question: A shop has four boxes of ten shirts. Does a four-part tape marked 10 in each part match the situation? Explain.
WorkedExamples.Method: Interpret the parts and labels, choose yes/no, then justify rather than returning only the product.
Steps: Identify FOUR store boxes.
Find FOUR equal parts in the independently redrawn tape.
Identify TEN shirts per box and label TEN in each part.
Answer YES and explain how each part stands for one box; teacher checks reasoning.
WorkedExamples.Answer: YES; four groups of ten represent forty shirts.
WorkedExamples.Check: 4 × 10 = 40; a bare 40 does not answer the original yes/no and explanation prompt.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Expecting an abstract multiplication expression before the source card sort.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The 2021 teacher narrative delays multiplication symbols until the lesson synthesis.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Lead with picture graphs, tape parts, card sort and drawings, then introduce 4 × 5 at the END.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Drawing three speed-limit marks rather than three groups of TWO.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The graph key multiplies every visible square by two real signs.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Show three separate tape parts each labelled 2; total six signs.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating 4 bags × 2 and 4 hands × 5 as one interchangeable task.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Each original Student Facing subpart requires a separate representation with different group sizes.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Represent four groups of 2 and four groups of 5 separately; teacher checks both.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Certifying the physical card sort based only on its numeric totals.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original source includes TWELVE A–L cards and asks pupils to justify pairing situations, drawings and diagrams.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use the source ZIP and teacher review of matching group structures; totals only support reasoning.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating a numerical 40 alone as completing the original Boxes of Shirts Cool-down.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original question requires yes/no verification of a diagram with four boxes, each holding ten shirts, AND an explanation of the correspondence.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Give YES for the four-part tape labelled ten, but explain how every partition represents one box; require teacher evaluation of reasoning.

SummaryPoints: Stage A source: first-edition 2021 teacher lesson and preparation HTML; original student task PDF four pages, original blackline deck two pages with twelve cards A–L directly inspected.
Warm-up (10m) six sock pairs; Activity 1 (15m) road-sign graph key 2 and speed-limit 3-part tape; independent second-category drawing.
Activity 2 (20m) original 12-card deck, precise five matching sets A–F–L, B–H–K, C–I, D–G and E–J; separate original four bags of two and four hands of five drawings; oral and teacher evidence.
Lesson synthesis (10m) FIRST teacher introduction of 4×5 from a four-by-five tape, followed by five-minute independently authored Cool-down.

Source original Boxes of Shirts Cool-down now verified against a public 2021-first-edition-based teacher guide: four boxes of ten match a four-part tape labelled ten (YES). Explanation is teacher-reviewed. The Edulytics extra Cool-down remains an optional separate exercise.
Prepare one original Equal Groups deck per pair; use MLR8/Engagement supports and keep the cards for Lesson 11. Suggested centers: Capture Squares Stage 4 and Five in a Row Stage 7.
